examples: The people at the front desk were really friendly.
She has a warm, friendly smile.
My new coworkers are a lot friendlier than my old ones.
The two countries have had friendly relations for decades.
I'm friendly with a few of the other parents at school.
We parted on friendly terms.
The senator gave her speech to a friendly crowd of supporters.
The new mayor has been friendly to small businesses.
Don't expect the reviewers to be friendly to a sequel.
It's a friendly little diner where everyone knows your name.
The office has a relaxed, friendly atmosphere.
The soldier was killed by friendly fire.
The damaged plane made it back to a friendly airfield.
It's just a friendly game — nobody's keeping score.
They made a friendly bet on the Super Bowl.
A little friendly competition keeps the team motivated.
We switched to environmentally friendly cleaning products.
The museum is very kid-friendly.
Is the hotel pet-friendly?

senses.head: Kind and pleasant to other people; behaving like a friend
examples: The people at the front desk were really friendly.
She has a warm, friendly smile.
My new coworkers are a lot friendlier than my old ones.

senses.head: On good terms with someone; not hostile
examples: The two countries have had friendly relations for decades.
I'm friendly with a few of the other parents at school.
We parted on friendly terms.

senses.head: Supportive of a person, a group or an idea; ready to agree or help
examples: The senator gave her speech to a friendly crowd of supporters.
The new mayor has been friendly to small businesses.
Don't expect the reviewers to be friendly to a sequel.

senses.head: Of a place or atmosphere: welcoming and comfortable
examples: It's a friendly little diner where everyone knows your name.
The office has a relaxed, friendly atmosphere.

senses.head: On your own side in a fight or a war
examples: The soldier was killed by friendly fire.
The damaged plane made it back to a friendly airfield.

senses.head: Done for fun or in a spirit of goodwill, not as serious competition
examples: It's just a friendly game — nobody's keeping score.
They made a friendly bet on the Super Bowl.
A little friendly competition keeps the team motivated.

senses.head: Not harmful to something, or well suited to a particular group; usually after another word
examples: We switched to environmentally friendly cleaning products.
The museum is very kid-friendly.
Is the hotel pet-friendly?

entries.position: both — a friendly neighbor, Our neighbors are friendly
entries.comparison: -er/-est or more/most — friendlier, friendliest, more friendly
entries.takes: to or toward a person (how you treat them: friendly to newcomers); to a group or an idea (supportive of it: friendly to small businesses); with a person (on good terms with them: friendly with the neighbors)
entries.contrast: There is no adverb friendlily. She smiled friendly is wrong; say She smiled in a friendly way or She gave me a friendly smile. After a linking verb the adjective is right: He seems friendly, Be friendly. Friendly to someone is about how you treat them; friendly with someone means you are on good terms: I'm friendly with her brother (мы с её братом приятели). In user-friendly, eco-friendly and kid-friendly the word means suitable for, or not harmful to.

examples: What a lovely view of the lake!
You look lovely in that dress.
It was the loveliest garden on the whole street.
We had a lovely evening — thanks for inviting us.
It was lovely to see you again.
The weather has been lovely all week.
Her parents are lovely people.
He's a lovely man and a great teacher.

senses.head: Beautiful or very attractive to look at
examples: What a lovely view of the lake!
You look lovely in that dress.
It was the loveliest garden on the whole street.

senses.head: Very pleasant or enjoyable
examples: We had a lovely evening — thanks for inviting us.
It was lovely to see you again.
The weather has been lovely all week.

senses.head: Of a person: kind, friendly and easy to like
examples: Her parents are lovely people.
He's a lovely man and a great teacher.

entries.position: both — a lovely view, The view is lovely
entries.comparison: -er/-est or more/most — lovelier, loveliest, more lovely
entries.contrast: There is no adverb lovelily: She sings lovely is wrong; say She sings beautifully. lovely has nothing to do with being in love or being loved: влюблённый is in love, любимый is favorite or beloved. It is far more frequent in British speech; Americans use it too, but nice, great and beautiful are more usual in casual talk.

examples: After his wife died, he felt terribly lonely.
Moving to a new city can be lonely at first.
It was the loneliest year of my life.
The car broke down on a lonely stretch of highway in Nevada.
The cabin sits on a lonely hillside miles from town.
A lonely figure walked along the empty beach.
One lonely light was still on in the office building.

senses.head: Unhappy because you are alone or have no friends; or, of a time or a life, spent that way
examples: After his wife died, he felt terribly lonely.
Moving to a new city can be lonely at first.
It was the loneliest year of my life.

senses.head: Of a place: far from where people live and seldom visited
examples: The car broke down on a lonely stretch of highway in Nevada.
The cabin sits on a lonely hillside miles from town.

senses.head: Standing or moving alone, with nobody or nothing else nearby
examples: A lonely figure walked along the empty beach.
One lonely light was still on in the office building.

entries.position: both — a lonely old man, He felt lonely
entries.comparison: -er/-est or more/most — lonelier, loneliest, more lonely
entries.contrast: alone means without other people — a plain fact — and it is predicative only: She lives alone, never an alone woman. lonely means sad because you are alone or have no friends: You can be alone without being lonely. lone goes only before a noun and means the only one: a lone tree, a lone gunman. There is no adverb lonelily; rephrase: She sat by herself, feeling lonely.

examples: Their kids are bright and lively.
At ninety, she's still as lively as ever.
He was the liveliest person at the party.
The neighborhood has a lively bar scene.
The market gets livelier on weekends.
The proposal led to a lively debate at the town meeting.
The class discussion got pretty lively.
She has a lively imagination.
He took a lively interest in local politics.
The band played a lively polka.
The song has a lively, catchy beat.
The kitchen was painted in lively shades of yellow and green.
A lively print can brighten up a plain room.

senses.head: Full of energy; cheerful and active
examples: Their kids are bright and lively.
At ninety, she's still as lively as ever.
He was the liveliest person at the party.

senses.head: Of a place or an event: busy, with a lot happening
examples: The neighborhood has a lively bar scene.
The market gets livelier on weekends.

senses.head: Of a discussion or debate: full of strong opinions and eager talk
examples: The proposal led to a lively debate at the town meeting.
The class discussion got pretty lively.

senses.head: Of the mind, interest or imagination: quick, strong and active
examples: She has a lively imagination.
He took a lively interest in local politics.

senses.head: Of music or dancing: fast and cheerful
examples: The band played a lively polka.
The song has a lively, catchy beat.

senses.head: Of colors: bright and strong
examples: The kitchen was painted in lively shades of yellow and green.
A lively print can brighten up a plain room.

entries.position: both — a lively debate, The debate got lively
entries.comparison: -er/-est or more/most — livelier, liveliest, more lively
entries.contrast: Pronounced LYV-lee, with the vowel of five, not the vowel of the verb live. Keep three words apart: alive = not dead, predicative only (The fish is still alive); live (LYV) = happening now or not recorded, before a noun (live music, a live broadcast); lively = full of energy (a lively crowd). A live concert is not recorded; a lively concert is energetic. There is no adverb livelily; say in a lively way.

examples: It was a silly mistake, and it cost us the game.
Don't be silly — of course you can come.
That's the silliest excuse I've ever heard.
The kids made silly faces for the camera.
We all wore silly hats to the party.
He gets sillier the more tired he is.
They had a fight over something silly.
It's just a silly little gift.
The lecture bored me silly.
The movie scared the kids silly.
We laughed ourselves silly.

senses.head: Showing poor judgment; foolish
examples: It was a silly mistake, and it cost us the game.
Don't be silly — of course you can come.
That's the silliest excuse I've ever heard.

senses.head: Playful and not serious, in a way meant to be funny
examples: The kids made silly faces for the camera.
We all wore silly hats to the party.
He gets sillier the more tired he is.

senses.head: Small and unimportant; not worth worrying about
examples: They had a fight over something silly.
It's just a silly little gift.

senses.head: Into a dazed or helpless state; only after verbs such as bore, scare and laugh
examples: The lecture bored me silly.
The movie scared the kids silly.
We laughed ourselves silly.

entries.position: both — a silly mistake, Don't be silly; the 'bored silly' sense only after a verb
entries.comparison: -er/-est or more/most — sillier, silliest, more silly
entries.takes: of + a person + to-infinitive (judging the person: It was silly of me to forget); for + a person + to-infinitive (the plan makes no sense: It's silly for us to take two cars)
entries.contrast: There is no adverb sillily in normal use: say in a silly way, or use a linking verb: Stop acting silly. silly is milder and friendlier than stupid: calling an idea silly is teasing, calling it stupid is an insult. To judge a person, the pattern is It was silly of you, not silly from you.

examples: They painted the house an ugly shade of brown.
Honestly, I think the new stadium is ugly.
That's the ugliest sweater I've ever seen.
Things got ugly when the police arrived.
There was an ugly scene outside the bar.
The crowd was in an ugly mood.
Someone started an ugly rumor about her.
The trial exposed an ugly side of the town's history.

senses.head: Unpleasant to look at
examples: They painted the house an ugly shade of brown.
Honestly, I think the new stadium is ugly.
That's the ugliest sweater I've ever seen.

senses.head: Of a situation or mood: unpleasant and threatening, likely to turn violent
examples: Things got ugly when the police arrived.
There was an ugly scene outside the bar.
The crowd was in an ugly mood.

senses.head: Morally unpleasant; cruel or offensive
examples: Someone started an ugly rumor about her.
The trial exposed an ugly side of the town's history.

entries.position: both — an ugly building, The building is ugly
entries.comparison: -er/-est or more/most — uglier, ugliest, more ugly
entries.contrast: There is no adverb uglily: say in an ugly way. Said of a person, ugly is much harsher than Russian некрасивый; Americans soften it to not very attractive or plain. In turn ugly and get ugly it means dangerous or violent, not unattractive: The protest turned ugly.

examples: An elderly woman asked me to help with her bags.
The program delivers hot meals to elderly residents.
Her father is elderly and can't drive anymore.
He still drives an elderly Buick.
Our elderly laptop takes five minutes to start up.

senses.head: Of a person: old; a polite word
examples: An elderly woman asked me to help with her bags.
The program delivers hot meals to elderly residents.
Her father is elderly and can't drive anymore.

senses.head: Of a thing: old and no longer working well; used humorously
examples: He still drives an elderly Buick.
Our elderly laptop takes five minutes to start up.

entries.position: both — an elderly neighbor, My parents are elderly now
entries.comparison: more/most — more elderly, most elderly, both rare; very elderly is the usual way to grade it
entries.contrast: elderly is a polite word for people who are old; old is plainer and can sound blunt about a person, and many Americans now prefer older (older adults) or senior. It is not a comparative: my older brother or my elder brother is старший брат, never my elderly brother. It is not an adverb either. The elderly (пожилые люди as a group) is a noun use.

examples: The old roof needed costly repairs.
Treating the disease is extremely costly.
Flying turned out to be costlier than driving.
Leaving the door unlocked was a costly mistake.
The delay proved costly for the company.
The fumble was the costliest error of the game.

senses.head: Costing a lot of money
examples: The old roof needed costly repairs.
Treating the disease is extremely costly.
Flying turned out to be costlier than driving.

senses.head: Causing a serious loss, damage or suffering
examples: Leaving the door unlocked was a costly mistake.
The delay proved costly for the company.
The fumble was the costliest error of the game.

entries.position: both — costly repairs, The repairs were costly
entries.comparison: -er/-est or more/most — costlier, costliest, more costly
entries.contrast: For prices in stores and restaurants, expensive is the everyday word: an expensive restaurant, not usually a costly restaurant. costly is more formal and goes with repairs, delays, lawsuits and mistakes, where it often means causing loss: a costly error = ошибка, которая дорого обошлась. There is no adverb costlily.

examples: Some wild mushrooms are deadly.
Fentanyl is far deadlier than heroin.
It was the deadliest hurricane in fifty years.
The two gangs were deadly rivals.
They had been deadly enemies since high school.
He's a deadly shooter from three-point range.
She hit the target with deadly accuracy.
A deadly silence fell over the room.
She was in deadly earnest about quitting.
The first hour of the movie is deadly.
Budget meetings can be absolutely deadly.

senses.head: Able or likely to cause death
examples: Some wild mushrooms are deadly.
Fentanyl is far deadlier than heroin.
It was the deadliest hurricane in fifty years.

senses.head: Of enemies or a conflict: extreme and aiming to destroy the other side
examples: The two gangs were deadly rivals.
They had been deadly enemies since high school.

senses.head: Extremely accurate or effective
examples: He's a deadly shooter from three-point range.
She hit the target with deadly accuracy.

senses.head: Complete or total; with a few nouns such as silence and earnest
examples: A deadly silence fell over the room.
She was in deadly earnest about quitting.

senses.head: Very boring; informal
examples: The first hour of the movie is deadly.
Budget meetings can be absolutely deadly.

entries.position: both — a deadly virus, The virus is deadly; deadly enemies only before a noun
entries.comparison: -er/-est or more/most — deadlier, deadliest, more deadly
entries.contrast: deadly = able to kill (a deadly disease, смертельный). deathly = like death (a deathly silence, deathly pale, мертвенный). dead = no longer alive. Before another adjective, deadly is an adverb meaning completely (deadly serious, deadly dull) — that use belongs to the adverb dictionary. In the seven deadly sins (семь смертных грехов) it means fatal to the soul, not to the body. There is no deadlily.

examples: He was too cowardly to tell her the truth himself.
Don't be so cowardly — just go talk to her.
It was the most cowardly thing I've ever seen anyone do.
The mayor called the bombing a cowardly attack on innocent people.
Breaking up by text is a cowardly way to end things.

senses.head: Lacking courage; too afraid to face danger or difficulty
examples: He was too cowardly to tell her the truth himself.
Don't be so cowardly — just go talk to her.
It was the most cowardly thing I've ever seen anyone do.

senses.head: Of an act: done so as to avoid risk to yourself, often by attacking people who cannot fight back
examples: The mayor called the bombing a cowardly attack on innocent people.
Breaking up by text is a cowardly way to end things.

entries.position: both — a cowardly act, It was cowardly
entries.contrast: coward is the noun, so it needs an article: He's a coward or He's cowardly, never He is coward. Though it ends in -ly, cowardly is not an adverb in modern English: He ran away like a coward, not He ran away cowardly.

examples: Her desk is always neat and orderly.
The books were lined up in orderly rows.
Please leave the building in an orderly fashion.
The protest was peaceful and orderly.
The transfer of power was more orderly than people expected.
She has a very orderly mind.
He lived a quiet, orderly life.

senses.head: Neatly arranged, with everything in its place
examples: Her desk is always neat and orderly.
The books were lined up in orderly rows.

senses.head: Calm and well behaved, without confusion or disorder
examples: Please leave the building in an orderly fashion.
The protest was peaceful and orderly.
The transfer of power was more orderly than people expected.

senses.head: Of a person, a mind or a way of life: organized, and following a regular system
examples: She has a very orderly mind.
He lived a quiet, orderly life.

entries.position: both — orderly rows, The room was neat and orderly
entries.contrast: There is no adverb form: Leave the building orderly is wrong; say in an orderly way or in an orderly fashion. An orderly (санитар в больнице) is a noun. The legal phrase disorderly conduct (нарушение общественного порядка) is common in American news.

examples: Please respond in a timely manner.
We appreciate your timely payment.
Thanks for the timely reminder — I almost forgot.
Her book on artificial intelligence couldn't be more timely.
The documentary is especially timely in an election year.

senses.head: Done or happening at the right time, or without delay
examples: Please respond in a timely manner.
We appreciate your timely payment.
Thanks for the timely reminder — I almost forgot.

senses.head: Dealing with something that matters right now; topical
examples: Her book on artificial intelligence couldn't be more timely.
The documentary is especially timely in an election year.

entries.position: both — mostly before a noun: a timely reminder; also The warning was timely
entries.contrast: timely is not an adverb: Please pay timely is wrong; say pay on time or, in formal writing, in a timely manner. The opposite untimely is mostly met in an untimely death (безвременная смерть). Russian актуальный is often timely or topical — never actual, which means фактический.

entries.meaning: Kind, warm and protective, like a good mother. ---
examples: An older, motherly nurse held my hand the whole time.
She's always been motherly toward the younger players.
Nobody in the office is more motherly than our receptionist.
entries.position: both — motherly advice, She was very motherly toward the new nurses
entries.contrast: motherly describes warm, caring behavior like a good mother's. maternal is the classifying word for anything connected with mothers: maternal health, and my maternal grandmother (бабушка по матери), never my motherly grandmother. There is no adverb: She looked after him in a motherly way.

entries.meaning: Kind, protective and ready to guide, like a good father. ---
examples: My boss gave me some fatherly advice about saving money.
He put a fatherly arm around the boy's shoulders.
The old coach was more fatherly than strict.
entries.position: both — fatherly advice, The coach was fatherly toward his players
entries.contrast: fatherly describes kind, guiding behavior like a good father's. paternal is the classifying word for anything connected with fathers: my paternal grandfather (дедушка по отцу), never my fatherly grandfather. There is no adverb: He talked to me in a fatherly way.

entries.meaning: Showing the love, loyalty or support expected between brothers. ---
examples: Philadelphia calls itself the City of Brotherly Love.
He gave his younger teammate a brotherly slap on the back.
Their rivalry was more brotherly than bitter.
entries.position: both — brotherly love, His concern was purely brotherly
entries.contrast: fraternal is the formal, classifying word: fraternal twins (разнояйцевые близнецы), a fraternal organization. For sisters the word is sisterly. There is no adverb: He treated me like a brother.

examples: The article appeared in a scholarly journal.
The book is scholarly but still easy to read.
It's the most scholarly biography of Lincoln to date.
He was a quiet, scholarly man who read Greek for fun.
Her scholarly manner made the students take her seriously.

senses.head: Of writing or work: based on serious academic research
examples: The article appeared in a scholarly journal.
The book is scholarly but still easy to read.
It's the most scholarly biography of Lincoln to date.

senses.head: Of a person: having a lot of knowledge from serious study, and fond of study
examples: He was a quiet, scholarly man who read Greek for fun.
Her scholarly manner made the students take her seriously.

entries.position: both — a scholarly journal, The book is scholarly but easy to read
entries.contrast: Russian научный splits in English. scientific is about the sciences and their methods (a scientific experiment); scholarly is about serious academic research in any field, especially the humanities (a scholarly book on Tolstoy); academic is about universities in general. In American English a scholar is учёный or a student with a scholarship, never a schoolchild.

entries.meaning: Done slowly and in a relaxed way, without hurrying. ---
examples: We took a leisurely walk along the beach.
Sunday breakfast is always a leisurely affair at our house.
The second half of the trip was more leisurely.
entries.position: both — mostly before a noun: a leisurely lunch; also The pace was leisurely
entries.contrast: Unlike most -ly adjectives, it is also an adverb: They strolled leisurely along the river is correct but bookish, and Americans usually say at a leisurely pace. Most Americans say LEE-zhur-lee; LEZH-ur-lee is also heard in the US, and LEZH-uh-lee is British. leisurely is about speed, not free time: свободное время is free time or leisure time.

examples: The choir sang of angels and the heavenly host.
Our heavenly Father, hear our prayer.
Galileo studied the moons of Jupiter and other heavenly bodies.
This chocolate cake is heavenly.
After the long hike, a hot shower felt heavenly.
I can't imagine anything more heavenly than a week at the beach.

senses.head: Of or from heaven, in religion; or in the sky, in the phrase heavenly bodies
examples: The choir sang of angels and the heavenly host.
Our heavenly Father, hear our prayer.
Galileo studied the moons of Jupiter and other heavenly bodies.

senses.head: Very pleasant; delightful
examples: This chocolate cake is heavenly.
After the long hike, a hot shower felt heavenly.
I can't imagine anything more heavenly than a week at the beach.

entries.position: both — heavenly bodies only before a noun; The cake was heavenly
entries.comparison: more/most — more heavenly in the 'delightful' sense; not gradable when it means 'of heaven'
entries.contrast: A heavenly body is a star, planet or moon (небесное тело), not a beautiful person. Russian небесный is heavenly mainly in religion and in heavenly bodies; for the color of the sky say sky blue, and science uses celestial. In everyday speech heavenly is mostly about food, smells and comfort: That bed is heavenly.

examples: A ghostly figure appeared at the end of the hallway.
The fog gave the streetlights a ghostly glow.
Under the hospital lights her face looked more ghostly than ever.
We heard ghostly footsteps in the attic.
The wind made a ghostly moaning sound through the trees.

senses.head: Pale, faint or hard to see, like a ghost
examples: A ghostly figure appeared at the end of the hallway.
The fog gave the streetlights a ghostly glow.
Under the hospital lights her face looked more ghostly than ever.

senses.head: Strange and frightening, as if caused by a ghost
examples: We heard ghostly footsteps in the attic.
The wind made a ghostly moaning sound through the trees.

entries.position: both — mostly before a noun: a ghostly figure; also Her face looked ghostly
entries.contrast: Do not confuse it with ghastly (GAST-lee), which means horrible or very bad: a ghastly accident, a ghastly mistake. ghostly means like a ghost. Neither word is an adverb.

examples: The monks gave up all their worldly possessions.
He left all his worldly goods to his niece.
She seemed so worldly to us small-town kids.
He was older and more worldly than the other students.
A year in Paris made her more worldly.

senses.head: Connected with ordinary material life and possessions rather than with religion or the spirit
examples: The monks gave up all their worldly possessions.
He left all his worldly goods to his niece.

senses.head: Experienced and knowledgeable about life, people and society
examples: She seemed so worldly to us small-town kids.
He was older and more worldly than the other students.
A year in Paris made her more worldly.

entries.position: both — worldly goods only before a noun; She was older and more worldly
entries.contrast: worldly does not mean мировой or всемирный. For those use world before a noun (a world record, world history), worldwide or global: world-famous (всемирно известный), never worldly famous. worldly is about material life (мирской) or experience of life (искушённый).

examples: She takes a daily walk after lunch.
There are three daily flights to Denver.
The manager sends us daily updates on the project.
The daily rate for the rental car is $45.
Try to stay under the recommended daily amount of sugar.
The daily high was 94 degrees.
Phones have become part of daily life.
The pandemic changed our daily routines.

senses.head: Happening, done or published every day, or every working day
examples: She takes a daily walk after lunch.
There are three daily flights to Denver.
The manager sends us daily updates on the project.

senses.head: Calculated for one day
examples: The daily rate for the rental car is $45.
Try to stay under the recommended daily amount of sugar.
The daily high was 94 degrees.

senses.head: Belonging to ordinary life as it goes on day after day
examples: Phones have become part of daily life.
The pandemic changed our daily routines.

entries.position: attributive only — a daily walk; after a verb English uses the adverb: I walk daily
entries.contrast: The same spelling is also an adverb (The museum is open daily) and a noun (a daily — ежедневная газета). Keep apart everyday, one word and an adjective (everyday clothes, повседневный), and every day, two words and an adverb phrase (I wear it every day). Daily life and everyday life both mean повседневная жизнь.

examples: We have a weekly team meeting on Mondays.
She writes a weekly column for the local paper.
The weekly farmers market runs until October.
His weekly paycheck barely covers the rent.
The show topped the weekly ratings again.

senses.head: Happening, done or published once a week
examples: We have a weekly team meeting on Mondays.
She writes a weekly column for the local paper.
The weekly farmers market runs until October.

senses.head: Calculated for one week
examples: His weekly paycheck barely covers the rent.
The show topped the weekly ratings again.

entries.position: attributive only — a weekly meeting; after a verb English uses the adverb: We meet weekly
entries.contrast: Also an adverb (The magazine comes out weekly) and a noun (a weekly — еженедельник). biweekly is ambiguous — twice a week or every two weeks — so Americans often say every other week or twice a week to be clear.

examples: The monthly rent is due on the first.
The library holds a monthly book discussion.
I set up automatic monthly payments for my phone bill.
A monthly subway pass costs $132.
Her monthly income went up after the promotion.

senses.head: Happening, done, paid or published once a month
examples: The monthly rent is due on the first.
The library holds a monthly book discussion.
I set up automatic monthly payments for my phone bill.

senses.head: Calculated for one month, or valid for one month
examples: A monthly subway pass costs $132.
Her monthly income went up after the promotion.

entries.position: attributive only — a monthly payment; after a verb English uses the adverb: We pay monthly
entries.contrast: Also an adverb (The bill is paid monthly) and a noun (a monthly — ежемесячный журнал). bimonthly can mean twice a month or every two months; every other month avoids the doubt.

examples: Don't skip your yearly checkup.
The town's yearly fireworks show draws huge crowds.
Her yearly salary is about $60,000.
A yearly subscription saves you twenty percent.

senses.head: Happening once a year
examples: Don't skip your yearly checkup.
The town's yearly fireworks show draws huge crowds.

senses.head: Calculated for one year
examples: Her yearly salary is about $60,000.
A yearly subscription saves you twenty percent.

entries.position: attributive only — a yearly checkup; after a verb English uses the adverb: The fee is paid yearly
entries.contrast: annual is the more common and more formal word, especially in business: an annual report, annual income. yearly is the everyday alternative, and it is also an adverb. The vowel is the one in year (YEER-lee), not the one in early (UR-lee).

examples: There's an hourly bus to the airport.
The station gives hourly traffic updates.
The hourly wage for the job is $18.
Most of the store's hourly employees work part-time.
Lawyers at the firm charge an hourly rate of $400.

senses.head: Happening once every hour
examples: There's an hourly bus to the airport.
The station gives hourly traffic updates.

senses.head: Calculated or paid by the hour
examples: The hourly wage for the job is $18.
Most of the store's hourly employees work part-time.
Lawyers at the firm charge an hourly rate of $400.

entries.position: attributive only — an hourly wage; after a verb English uses the adverb: The bus runs hourly
entries.contrast: The h is silent, so the word takes an: an hourly rate, not a hourly rate. American hourly workers are paid by the hour, as opposed to salaried ones who get a fixed yearly amount. Also an adverb: The news is updated hourly.

entries.meaning: Happening every night or every evening. ---
examples: My parents never miss the nightly news.
The theater has nightly shows through August.
The nightly fireworks at the park start at nine.
entries.position: attributive only — the nightly news; after a verb English uses the adverb: The show runs nightly
entries.contrast: It means every night or every evening, not simply ночной. For something that happens at night, use night or nighttime before a noun: a night flight, nighttime temperatures. Also an adverb: The show runs nightly. It sounds the same as knightly (рыцарский).

examples: I caught the early bus to work.
She moved to Chicago in her early twenties.
The disease is easiest to treat in its earliest stages.
You're early — the party doesn't start until eight.

senses.head: Near the beginning of a day, a period, a process or someone's life
examples: I caught the early bus to work.

senses.head: Arriving, happening or done before the usual, expected or planned time
examples: You're early — the party doesn't start until eight.

entries.type: age — a time word: near the beginning, or before the usual time
entries.position: both — an early train, The train was early
entries.takes: for + an event or a time (early for the meeting); to-infinitive (too early to tell)
entries.contrast: The same form is also an adverb — an early flight (adjective), We left early (adverb) — and there is no earlily. early compares with the usual or planned time (рано, раньше срока); soon means a short time from now (скоро): Come early = приходите пораньше, Come soon = приходите поскорее. Before a time word it needs no of: in early May, in the early 1990s, not in the early of May.

examples: Jerusalem is a holy city for three religions.

senses.head: Connected with God or religion; sacred
examples: Jerusalem is a holy city for three religions.

senses.head: Of a person: deeply religious and morally good
examples: Her grandmother was a holy woman who went to Mass every day.

senses.head: Used for emphasis in a few informal phrases, such as a holy terror and a holy mess
examples: Their two-year-old is a holy terror.
The kitchen was a holy mess after the party.

entries.position: both — holy water, This ground is holy; a holy terror only before a noun
entries.contrast: holy is not the title of a saint: Saint Peter, St. Nicholas, never Holy Peter; a holy person is a saint. Three words sound alike: holy (святой), wholly (полностью, an adverb) and holey (дырявый). Holy cow! and Holy smoke! are exclamations, not this adjective. holier-than-thou means acting morally better than everyone else.

senses.head: Happy, cheerful and friendly
examples: Santa is usually drawn as a fat, jolly man with a white beard.

senses.head: Of an occasion: enjoyable and festive
examples: The whole family had a jolly time at the holiday party.

entries.position: both — a jolly man, He was jolly
entries.contrast: jolly as an adverb meaning very (jolly good, jolly well) is British and sounds old-fashioned or jokey to Americans. In American English the adjective is most familiar from Christmas (a jolly old elf, a holly jolly Christmas); in everyday talk cheerful is more common. There is no adverb jollily in normal use: say laughed cheerfully or laughed heartily.

examples: Get your smelly gym socks out of my car!
The fridge is getting smelly — we need to clean it out.
Blue cheese is one of the smelliest foods I know.
entries.position: both — smelly socks, The fridge is smelly
entries.contrast: smelly is always negative — it means the smell is bad, like вонючий, not like пахучий. For a pleasant smell say fragrant or sweet-smelling, or use the verb: The bread smells great. After the verb smell use an adjective, not an adverb: It smells bad, not It smells badly.

examples: The baby has curly red hair.

examples: The pig has a curly little tail.

entries.position: both — curly hair, His hair is curly
entries.contrast: English puts the adjective on the hair: She has curly hair or She's curly-haired; She is curly is heard but informal. curly means tight curls; wavy means loose waves (волнистый). In American computing, curly brackets are usually called braces { }.

senses.head: Full of bubbles

entries.position: both — a bubbly personality, She's so bubbly
entries.comparison: -er/-est or more/most — bubblier, bubbliest, more bubbly
entries.contrast: bubbly as a noun (a glass of bubbly) means champagne or sparkling wine — a noun, not this adjective. For drinks, American English usually says sparkling or carbonated: sparkling water. Calling a person bubbly is a compliment (жизнерадостная), used mostly about women and girls.

senses.head: Unfriendly; not warm in manner
examples: The proposal got a chilly reception from the board.

entries.position: both — a chilly morning, It's chilly outside
entries.contrast: It sounds the same as chili (перец чили, the American spelling), but chilly means cold in an unpleasant way — somewhere between cool and cold. For a person, English uses be: I'm chilly or I'm cold (мне зябко, мне холодно), not It's chilly to me.
